newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
PARLEYS ON FOR CONSENSUS CONGRESS PARLIAMENTARY PARTY CHIEF

Congress leaders held parleys to avoid a contest for the leadership of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP). A secret meeting between Congress chief Sitaram Kesri and Congress Working Committee (CWC) member Rajesh Pilot, followed by a call on the latter by Kesri's emissary Jitendra Prasad, were a pointer in this direction. Party sources said Kesri would also meet his rival and former Maharashtra chief minister Sharad Pawar in an effort to end the stalemate on the leadership issue. Both Pilot and Pawar are vying for the CPP leadership.
Business Standard
DIVIDEND PAYMENT BY PRIVATE CORPORATES UP 25 % IN '95-96

The domestic corporate sector had a mixed year of dividend payment in fiscal 1995/96 (April-March). Some sectors like automobiles, cement, power and food processing were able to improve cash returns to their shareholders, while some others like sugar and breweries, cotton textiles and tobacco failed to match their 1994/95 payout. A recent study revealed the private corporate sector paid 37.97 billion rupees by way of dividend in 1995/96, up 24.6 percent from 30.46 billion rupees in 1994/95.
The Economic Times
NON-BANKING FINANCING CORPS FACE MINISTRY'S BLADE

Non-banking financial institutions (NBFCs), not registered with the registrar of companies, may soon have to undergo compulsory registration. The government is considering appropriate changes in the Companies Act. The finance ministry is also considering amendments in the Reserve Bank of India Act to ensure tighter control of NBFCs by the apex bank. The government is also looking at ways to give powers to the department of company affairs to keep a close watch on NBFCs.
TATA TELECOM, LUCENT, NELCO'S ITG TO TIE THE KNOT

The Tata-Lucent Technologies joint venture would be a 50:50 partnership, and is expected to be operational by April 1997. The venture is expected to be a merger of Tata Telecom, Lucent Technologies and Nelco's Information Technology Group (ITG), sources close to the deal said. The venture would allow Lucent, the erstwhile AT&T Network Systems, to hold 50 percent, while the two Indian entities, ITG and Tata Telecom, would constitute Tata's 50 percent. The new entity is expected to have a paid-up capital of about one billion rupees, and would probably be named Lucent-Tata Telecom India.
CREDIT RATING FIRMS TO STUDY STATE UNITS

The Disinvestment Commission has engaged the services of Crisil, Care and Icra to study the 40 public sector units (PSUs) referred to it by the core group of secretaries for possible disinvestment by the government. Commission chairman G.V. Ramakrishna said the three credit rating firms had been allotted different PSUs and they would analyse the units with reference to future profitability, technology levels and other relevant details. The commission chairman said they would also indicate the need for restructuring PSUs, wherever required.
PRIVATE POWER FIRMS MAY BE ALLOWED TO SELL EXCESS COAL

The government may allow private firms, which were allotted captive mines, to sell out excess coal. However, the private firms would be allowed to do so only if the reserves of mine so permit. The move has come in the wake of private mine operators' threat to give up the captive-mines allotted to them.
Financial Express
ARTHUR D LITTLE, ICICI TO MAKE RECAST FOR BPCL

The Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) has appointed Arthur D Little and the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India, to chalk out an organisational restructuring strategy. The move is aimed at restructuring BPCL to face the challenge posed by the decontrol of petroleum sector. They are expected to finalise their recommendations by March 1997. These recommendations will work as catalytic agents for improving the performance of the company in the decontrolled scenario.
NEW LIQUOR POLICY ON THE ANVIL

The government is in the process of reviewing the liquor policy with the aim of increasing licensed capacity. Sources said the government was considering cancellation of unutilised licences granted for potable alcohol and beer. The move to increase liquor capacity is a clear departure from the government's continued stance over the past two decades. The government is also considering a plan to allow existing manufacturers to expand their capacities in order to provide the industry with a level-playing field.
Business Standard
ORDINANCE TO POLICE DTH SERVICES PLANNED

The government plans to issue an ordinance as an additional regulatory measure to police the proposed direct to home (DTH) television services. The ordinance is likely to have clauses which will bring DTH operators and broadcasters operating from countries like Hong Kong and Singapore within the ambit of Indian law. It cannot, however, directly prosecute anybody starting a DTH service from foreign soil. A recent department of telecommunications' notification makes it mandatory to obtain a licence for receiving television signals from satellites above 4,800 MHz. Though many foreign companies are interested in launching a DTH network for India, only Rupert Murdoch's STAR TV looks a serious
NEW CIVIL AVIATION POLICY AWAITS CABINET APPROVAL

The civil aviation ministry has submitted the new civil aviation policy for government's consideration. The policy package contains the basic framework prepared by the ministry after detailed consultations with concerned sections of the industry. Sources said one of the most contentious issues was whether foreign airlines should be allowed to acquire equity in domestic airlines. The issue was closely linked with the fate of the proposed Tata-Singapore joint airlines venture for domestic operations in India, sources added.
The Observer
U.S. TELECOM COMMISSION ACCUSED OF UNFAIR PRACTICE

Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL), India's telecommunication administrator, said the U.S. Federal Communications Commission's (FCC) demand that developing countries, including India, should reduce international telephone charges and total accounting rates was a ploy to protect its interests. VSNL accused FCC of drawing up a strategy to increase business and profitability of the U.S. carriers at the cost of telecom administrations of developing countries, which, VSNL said, were already affected due to the practices legalised by the U.S. authority.
